content: Humility is often only a feigned submission, which we use to bend others to our will; it is an artifice of pride.
author: François de La Rochefoucauld
sourceWork: Memoirs of the Regency of Anne of Austria
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. True art and creative work are not about clever technique; they demand total emotional skin in the game. When you create safely to please an audience or avoid criticism, the work feels hollow and bloodless.

François de La Rochefoucauld understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Pouring your genuine spirit, vulnerability, and raw lived experience into what you make is what gives it enduring life. The work that resonates across centuries is always the work created with unapologetic personal truth.
reflectionPrompt: What hidden motive, insecurity, or fear might be silently driving your recent reactions?
